current.title: DomainSpec v2 first production release
current.purpose: Carry the accepted private repository-local system-builder and conformance CLI from owner-ratified business meaning through typed specification projection, architecture and composable-pattern enforcement, bounded formal validation, independently grounded generated verification, structural implementation analysis, directional cross-graph conformance, a clean release candidate, and the exact 14-step Body War pilot. This context is continuation authority, not production authorization.
current.next_move: FPR-01 and W1 are closed. FPR-02 remains split into independent backend and UI lanes. The 2026-07-23 BTE L0A/L0B-L8 route is validated. L0A was selected and implemented, but current byte proof is blocked. Backend execution next requires explicit selection of SWU-BTE-L0A-REPAIR-001 and a strict runtime context pack. Current publication verification and the validation-owner freeze both gate L0B. FPR-02U may resume SWU-UIP-005 independently. Production remains unauthorized.

visibility_context.next_move: After any authorized Craft or FPR manifest update, run the visibility roadmap builder documented in development/first-production-release/visibility/PLAN-TRANSPORT.md, then run the same command with `--check`. Route new material frontiers through the existing persistent research protocol; do not select or advance either FPR-02B or FPR-02U here.

fields.text: Product direction agreed
The release ambition and the capabilities it must eventually prove have been explicitly accepted.
Resolve contradictions in the project
Compare the roadmap, specifications, decisions, and code. For every disagreement, record what the team will follow and who approved it.
Separate backend and UI profile work
Give backend release work and required UI development separate owners, gates, receipts, and next moves without an implicit join.
Freeze the backend release promise
Define the exact backend profile, Body War pilot, claims, owners, negatives, rollback, origin, redaction, and stable digest.
Build the required UI profile
Continue the eleven-concept UI development profile and hand exact authority deltas to owners without blocking the backend release.
Connect business meaning to the Spec
Give business concepts governed identities and explicit mappings into the authoritative DomainSpec model.
Produce the authoritative Spec
Create the canonical machine-readable specification that every downstream check and generator will use.
Enforce architecture and composition
Reject implementations that violate the selected architecture rules or allowed composable patterns.
Check behavior with bounded formal models
Translate selected claims into reproducible state and relational checks with explicit bounds and limits.
Generate complete tests independently
Derive obligations separately from generated code, then generate a test engine that covers that declared denominator.
Compare implementation structure to the Spec
Extract what the code actually contains and map it to the Spec without trusting tags or generated claims alone.
Combine all conformance results
Join business-to-Spec, Spec-to-implementation, architecture, formal, and test evidence without collapsing uncertainty into a false pass.
Make Body War behave exactly as promised
Bring the Body War witness into conformance with the frozen functional, security, consent, and evidence contract.
Prepare release operations
Make CI, deployment, rollback, audit, redaction, revocation, and support part of the release proof.
Build a clean reproducible candidate
Build one identifiable candidate from pinned inputs and prove it again in clean CI rather than a prepared workstation.
Run the controlled Body War pilot
Exercise the candidate through the exact 14-step Body War path under controlled release conditions.
Prove the roadmap can continue without drift
Show that another authorized owner or agent can recover the same state, evidence, and next move without hidden context.
Accept the claims and authorize release
Named owners review the evidence, narrow unsupported statements, and decide whether release is justified.
